about: I Am the Captain Now is a tight close-up of the Somali pirate leader Muse, played by Barkhad Abdi, staring straight at the camera with wide eyes and two fingers pointed at his own face. In the film he says "Look at me. Look at me. I'm the captain now" to the ship's real captain, played by Tom Hanks, the moment the hijackers seize the bridge. As a meme it marks a hostile takeover of any kind: the cat that claims your desk chair, the intern who ends up running the meeting, the autocorrect that rewrites your message, or the side dish that becomes the main event.
origin: The scene is from Captain Phillips (2013), Paul Greengrass's film about the hijacking of the cargo ship Maersk Alabama. Abdi's delivery of the line earned him an Oscar nomination and turned the quote into a stock reaction image almost as soon as the movie came out.
usage:
The top box sets the scene, usually naming the newcomer and who it just pushed aside, often starting with "look at me". The bottom box finishes the line: "I'm the captain now" or a twist on it. The joke works best when the thing taking control is small, silly or supposed to be subordinate, because Muse's dead-serious stare makes the power grab feel absurdly dramatic.

Good targets are pets, kids, software updates, group chat admins, substitute teachers and anything that quietly took over your schedule. Keep the takeover concrete so the reader instantly sees who used to be in charge.
ideas: the cat after I stand up for one second
look at me, I'm the captain now
the intern who found the admin password
look at me, I'm the sysadmin now
the backup goalie in the final
my toddler holding the TV remote
look at me, I'm the captain now
aka: Look at Me I'm the Captain Now
